_comment: **Torchflowers growing wild, which vanilla never does** (design §7.1.2). Nothing in the game places
this flower: a sniffer digs the seed and a player plants the crop, so a torchflower standing in the
world is proof somebody wrote it there. That is what makes the scarab's first condition unforgeable,
and why the patch is ours rather than a vanilla feature we could have named.
**`simple_block`, because there is no patch feature left.** `minecraft:flower` and
`minecraft:random_patch` are both gone from the feature registry -- vanilla's own FLOWER_DEFAULT is a
`simple_block` now, and what used to be `tries`/`xz_spread` is done with placement modifiers instead.
A feature naming either of the old types is dropped at datapack load, which is silent.
The block is `minecraft:torchflower` -- the grown flower, not `torchflower_crop`, which is farmland-
bound and would pop off a jungle floor at its first neighbour update. `simple_block` asks
`canSurvive` before it places, so a flower that lands on stone or leaves simply does not appear.
26.3 takes the state straight: `simple_state_provider` is gone from the data, and `to_place` reads a
block state where it read a provider wrapping one.
